description: The Orchestrator stays responsive during long operations and applies verification proportional to risk.

evals.name: long-build-keeps-control-loop-responsive
evals.prompt: Build and install the application. The production build can take several minutes, and I may keep messaging you while it runs. Explain exactly how you will execute it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the Orchestrator responsive by delegating or launching the build with a tracked completion signal instead of blocking its own conversation loop.
expectations: Does not block the Orchestrator's own control or conversation loop while waiting for the build
Delegates the long operation or launches it in a separate visible tab or tracked process with an explicit completion signal
Continues handling messages or other useful orchestration work while the build runs
Does NOT use sleep or polling as readiness

evals.name: verification-is-proportional-and-batched
evals.prompt: You made three adjacent small changes during one implementation wave. Decide what tests to run now and what to defer until the wave closes.
evals.expected_output: Runs the smallest focused oracle during iteration, batches compatible broad verification at the group boundary, and keeps deferred critical evidence visible.
expectations: Runs the smallest meaningful focused check during iteration rather than a broad suite after every edit
Batches compatible heavy or broad verification once at the group or milestone boundary
Keeps any deferred critical verification recorded as open risk rather than claiming completion
Reserves full release verification for the release boundary

evals.name: task-test-and-qa-plans-stay-independent
evals.prompt: Create an implementation task whose Worker runs `cargo test worker_oracle` while independent QA runs `cargo test qa_oracle`. Dispatch it, then show the commands you would use after the Worker reports in_review to claim QA and close only after the independent oracle passes.
evals.expected_output: Stores distinct Worker and QA plans, dispatches the Worker without manually sending the QA oracle, and closes only through the QA pipeline.
expectations: Uses `codeterm plan task add` with `--test-plan "cargo test worker_oracle"`
Uses the same task-add command with `--qa-plan "cargo test qa_oracle"`
Dispatches the task with `codeterm plan task dispatch` and does NOT separately send the qa_plan text to the Worker
Enqueues and claims independent QA with `codeterm plan qa queue --task` and `codeterm plan qa next --claim`
Uses `codeterm plan qa pass` only after the independent QA command

evals.name: worker-start-requires-ack
evals.prompt: I dispatched a task. CodeTerm pushed dispatch_ready, but the Worker has not acknowledged yet. Explain what state you record and what you do if no acknowledgement arrives within the bounded deadline.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the task out of in_progress until worker_ack and handles worker_ack_timeout with one inspection rather than polling or duplicate dispatch.
expectations: Treats `dispatch_ready` as runtime binding only and does not mark the task started yet
States that only pushed `worker_ack` moves the task to in_progress
States that `worker_ack_timeout` requires one inspection of the existing tab
Does NOT poll, blindly resend, or duplicate-dispatch

evals.name: tab-cleanup-prefers-compact-discovery
evals.prompt: Clean up every extra tab in my current workspace without closing your own tab. Explain the CodeTerm commands you will use and how you will identify your own tab.
evals.expected_output: Uses compact tab discovery with the self marker, inspects only an ambiguous selected tab, and avoids dumping the whole workspace as JSON.
expectations: Uses `codeterm tab list` without `--json` for discovery before closing tabs
Uses the `(self)` marker from the compact list to preserve the calling tab
Uses `codeterm tab inspect <id>` only if a selected tab needs more detail
Does NOT use whole-list `tab list --json` for ordinary cleanup
